description: Fixed key/data/expected-MAC triples for the HMAC-BLAKE2s construction R-13-072 requires (docs/13-security-pairing.md), working around cryptography 2.9.0's Blake2s.blockLengthInBytes bug (32 instead of the correct RFC 7693 value, 64). Every MAC below was computed with a hand-rolled RFC 2104 HMAC over blake2 0.10.6's Blake2s256 (ipad/opad width 64, matching snow 0.10.0's own internal HashBLAKE2s::hmac()), then cross-checked against an independent Python hashlib.blake2s-based reference implementation. crates/herdr-relay/tests/hmac_blake2s_vectors.rs asserts every vector byte for byte; app/test/services/hmac_blake2s_vectors_test.dart (WP-14-b, not yet built) reads this same file as its own canonical source, per R-13-072.

vectors.name: zero_key_empty_data
vectors.note: Boundary case: a 32-byte all-zero key (Noise's chaining_key length) with empty data.

vectors.name: psk0_mix_key_and_hash_step
vectors.note: A real intermediate value from a live Noise_XXpsk0 handshake this session verified end to end (crates/herdr-relay/src/noise.rs, app/test/spike/noise_client_test.dart): key is the chaining key right after Initialize()/MixHash(prologue) for Noise_XXpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s with an empty prologue; data is psk_from_phrase("remedy-tapestry-hubcap-oversleep-jailbird-kinetic") (R-13-024). The expected MAC is the temp_key MixKeyAndHash's HKDF derives from them.

vectors.name: hkdf_expand_counter_byte
vectors.note: The Noise-spec HKDF's second HMAC call: key is the psk0 step's own temp_key (this file's psk0_mix_key_and_hash_step vector's expected_mac_hex), data is the single counter byte 0x01 HKDF-Expand appends. The expected MAC matches the chaining key this session's live handshake produced after the psk token.

vectors.name: sixty_four_byte_key
vectors.note: Boundary case at R-13-072's stated maximum: a key exactly 64 bytes long (0x00..0x3f), so ipad/opad XOR the key across their full width with no zero-padding remainder. Noise itself never passes a chaining_key this long (always 32 bytes), but the construction must still be correct at the boundary.

vectors.name: ascii_data
vectors.note: A human-readable data payload (the docs' own worked pairing phrase, docs/11-relay-protocol.md §8.1) with an arbitrary fixed 32-byte key, as a plain sanity case distinct from the handshake-derived vectors above.
